newsitem.title: USA: Digital expected to post Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: Digital expected to post Q1 loss.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp is expected to report on Tuesday a loss for the first quarter, due to weak European sales, its struggling personal computer unit and a restructuring of its sales force, analysts said.

After posting six consecutive quarterly profits, Digital stunned Wall Street with losses of $433 million or $2.87 a share in its fourth quarter ended June 30, including a $492 million restrucuturing charge for job cuts and plant closings.
The first quarter is usually slow for Digital because Europe, where the Maynard, Mass., computer manufacturer draws a disproportionate share of its sales, essentially takes the month of August off.

However, Europe has been hit by an economic slowdown which has cut capital expenditures, analysts said, just when Digital was reorganizing its worldwide sales force. Currency fluctuations are also likely to dampen earnings, they said.
"They got a transition of the sales force, the PCs are still negative and Europe is still dead in the water," said David Wu, an analyst with Chicago Corp.
"If anything, Europe looks even worse," after IBM's results, he added. Earlier Monday, International Business
Machines Corp reported that revenues for its most recent quarter from Europe were flat and were adversely affected by currency fluctuations.
Industry-wide price cuts in personal computers earlier this year and an inventory build-up hurt Digital's personal computer unit in the fourth quarter.
Enrico Pesatori, who joined Digital to head the personal computer unit and became heir apparent to Digital Chief Executive Robert Palmer, suddenly resigned in early July amid distribution problems.
Analysts said the PC unit is still struggling.
Wu said he expects Digital to report a loss of from $0.30 to $0.50 per share.
Terry Shannon, editor of "Shannon Knows DEC," an Ashland, Mass., newsletter, only expected losses of about $0.14 or $0.15 per share.
"They've pulled off an against-all-odds recovery in the past, and there's no reason to think they can't repeat it," Shannon said.

According to First Call, which monitors Wall Street earnings estimates, the consensus estimate for Digital's first quarter is a loss of $0.14 a share. It listed a range of a loss of $0.30 to a profit of $0.05.
The second quarter is traditionally a stronger one for Digital, and both Shannon and Wu said Digital had better report improved results then or Palmer's job could be in trouble.

"They (Digital's losses) better not be sustained, or I won't be following the company," Wu said. "Bob Palmer has been there for over four years. He better perform or I have lost interest. The Christmas quarter is very crucial."
Palmer told reporters and analysts in late July the PC unit would break even or be profitable by the end of the second quarter.

"I don't believe things are quite as bad as they look," Shannon said, adding that when he talked to Palmer a week-and-a-half ago, the CEO said Digital would break even or be profitable for the second quarter.
A Digital spokesman declined to comment on earnings estimates or Palmer's status with the company.
